g.desc: {"kind":"workflow","id":"boot","title":"Host load — when the tools are registered","description":"Registration happens once per host process, not per chat turn. Since 0.5.63 every registration takes its model-facing description from one composer, so the registry and MCP cannot disagree.","steps":[{"id":"load","title":"The plugin applies its configuration","description":"[tool-mode](#boot) reads [the catalog and config](#catalog): which models the operator enabled, which extensions are installed, and whether unavailable models may be exposed at all.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(boot -> catalog)[0]"},{"edge":"(boot -> promptsec)[0]"}]},{"id":"register","title":"Control tools and contract tools enter the registry","description":"The host always registers its control surface; every enabled model binds its contract tool. A model whose route cannot run stays unregistered unless `exposeUnavailable` is on. [The composer](#composer) turns the declared text into the model-facing description (purpose, when to use, when not to use, inputs/outputs, limits, one example).","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(boot -> control)[0]"},{"edge":"(control -> tools)[0]"},{"edge":"(catalog -> contracts)[0]"},{"edge":"(catalog -> composer)[0]"},{"edge":"(composer -> contracts)[0]"},{"edge":"(contracts -> tools)[0]"}]},{"id":"activate","title":"Installed extensions publish their tools","description":"The extension lifecycle activates installed packages. Manifest tools and declarative recipe tools register through [the composer](#composer); the readiness fact decides whether a model-backed tool is callable. Manifest skills are contributed too and registered by the host hook.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(lifecycle -> readiness)[0]"},{"edge":"(lifecycle -> extools)[0]"},{"edge":"(extools -> composer)[0]"},{"edge":"(composer -> extools)[0]"},{"edge":"(extools -> tools)[0]"},{"edge":"(lifecycle -> extskills)[0]"},{"edge":"(extskills -> prompt)[0]"},{"edge":"(readiness -> exec)[0]"}]},{"id":"guide","title":"Skills teach when to use the tools","description":"The plugin registers one skill per catalog model when skills are enabled, and since 0.5.63 also registers the skills declared by extension manifests (resolving `requiresTools` tool ids through the manifest before gating). The harness advertises the skill catalog so the model can learn usage before calling anything.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(skills -> prompt)[0]"},{"edge":"(extskills -> prompt)[1]"}]}]}

g.desc: {"kind":"workflow","id":"turn","title":"One model step — what the agent sees and how it decides","description":"This repeats for every model step of every turn. Discovery through the control tools and Code Mode is detailed in the next workflow.","steps":[{"id":"assemble","title":"The prompt collects the model-facing schemas","description":"[The tools service](#tools) wires every registered tool into [system prompt assembly](#prompt) as name, description and parameters. The description is the composed text, not the raw catalog or contract string: it carries when to use, when not to use, limits and one example. Registration is the filter; readiness is not. The PTC and tools-SDK sections describe Code Mode.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(tools -> prompt)[0]"},{"edge":"(skills -> prompt)[0]"},{"edge":"(promptsec -> prompt)[0]"}]},{"id":"pin","title":"The agent loop pins that list in the request header","description":"The loop compares the assembled tools with the header in force. The header is the model-facing list; a schema or description change is an explicit additions-or-removals event, not a silent mutation.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(prompt -> loop)[0]"},{"edge":"(loop -> header)[0]"},{"edge":"(header -> model)[0]"}]},{"id":"decide","title":"The model chooses among the tools it can see","description":"The model sees names, composed descriptions, parameter schemas and skill text, never the UI cards. It decides: answer without a tool, call a visible tool directly, load a skill first, or compose tools through Code Mode using the control tools. Embedding-family descriptions name the sibling to choose instead, so the choice is not left to the name alone.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(model -> exec)[0]"}]},{"id":"run","title":"The call executes through the registry","description":"Execution is the only place readiness is enforced. A failed or needs-preparation deployment refuses with its reason; prepared-cold loads the engine on first use; a contract tool dispatches to its provider.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(exec -> readiness)[0]"},{"edge":"(readiness -> engines)[0]"},{"edge":"(engines -> exec)[0]"},{"edge":"(exec -> model)[0]"}]},{"id":"next","title":"The step settles and the header may change","description":"The result becomes context for the next step. If the tool set changed through activation or install, the loop logs a new header; otherwise the pinned list stays identical. Heavy-schema deferral is an opt-in flag (off by default): it marks selected schemas with deferLoading at registration, and the activation caveat is documented.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(exec -> model)[0]"},{"edge":"(loop -> header)[0]"},{"edge":"(header -> model)[0]"}]}]}

g.desc: {"kind":"workflow","id":"codemode","title":"Code Mode — discovering tools the model cannot see directly","description":"Code Mode is the second discovery path: the model sees tool_mode_run but not the bindings, so it must ask what exists.","steps":[{"id":"open","title":"The program door is visible","description":"[tool_mode_run](#control) is a normal tool. Its description tells the model that Tool Mode tools are only reachable through a program.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(model -> control)[0]"}]},{"id":"list","title":"Ask what can be called here","description":"`tool_mode_list` returns the permitted surface with readiness. `tool_mode_describe` returns the full schema, semantics, examples and unsupported cases for the selected names. Registered tools and unavailable models come back in separate lists (P4); only tools may be bound in a program.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(model -> control)[1]"},{"edge":"(control -> tools)[0]"},{"edge":"(tools -> control)[0]"},{"edge":"(model -> control)[2]"},{"edge":"(control -> model)[0]"}]},{"id":"program","title":"Write a program against the discovered bindings","description":"The program's calls are real registry calls, so each sub-call passes the same readiness gate and produces its own receipt.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(model -> exec)[0]"},{"edge":"(exec -> readiness)[0]"},{"edge":"(readiness -> engines)[0]"},{"edge":"(exec -> model)[0]"}]}]}

g.desc: {"kind":"workflow","id":"external","title":"MCP — when a non-DSH client calls the same tools","description":"The MCP surface is a third consumer, not part of the model loop. Since 0.5.63 it publishes the SAME composed description as the registry, so an external client and the model read one text.","steps":[{"id":"list","title":"The external client asks what is exported","description":"The MCP host publishes the plugin's contract tools and extension contributions, with withheld tools carrying their reason; the advertised description comes from [the composer](#composer).","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(mcp -> tools)[0]"},{"edge":"(tools -> mcp)[0]"},{"edge":"(composer -> mcp)[0]"}]},{"id":"call","title":"The external client invokes a tool","description":"The call enters the same execution pipeline as a model call, so readiness and receipts are not weaker on this path.","layer":0,"items":[{"edge":"(mcp -> exec)[0]"},{"edge":"(exec -> readiness)[0]"}]}]}
